newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark to focus on openess, environment at IGC.
newsitem.headline: Denmark to focus on openess, environment at IGC.

text.p: Denmark's government unveiled a draft policy document on Friday calling for tighter environmental legislation and more openness in the workings of the 15-member European Union (EU).

The document, setting out Denmark's latest thoughts on a reform of the workings of the EU, is to be presented to the current IGC (intergovernmental conference) on the future of the bloc, the government said.
The IGC, which started in March and meets monthly, is due to complete its deliberations next year.
The Danish government draft follows an earlier statement listing the fight against unemployment and expansion to embrace eastern European countries as major IGC priorities for Denmark.
On environmental issues, the Danish government lists a four-point programme it intends to press for to gain inclusion in the final IGC pact.

It calls for EU to incorporate the targets of the 1992 Rio Conference on improving the global environment into its own treaty stipulations and pay more attention to environmental issues in all aspects of the bloc's activity.

"Environmental considerations must be present to a much greater degree in EU's various areas of co-operation and the EU should incorporate into its new treaty clauses guaranteeing an acceptable development of the environment," the document said.
Health, safety and environmental considerations must also be given greater priority in the Single European Market, the document said, and all EU member states should impose environmental taxes.
It said that environmental guarantees should be precisely defined, clearly setting out the duties and responsibilities of the European Council, the European Commission and Parliament.

On openness, the Danish government said in its IGC draft that it would urge that transparency be laid down as one of the EU's basic principles in the new treaty, impinging on all aspects of the bloc's activity.
"The basic principle of transparency ought to be set out at the very beginning of the new treaty," the government said.
"We propose introducing concrete rules as regards openness in the EU, with provisions calling for public access to its legislative, internal and legal activity," it said.

"The Danish government wants to see a new treaty stipulation on transparency in EU lawmaking procedure in the form of open council debates and the publication of ballot results. The idea is to bring the bloc's legislative process more in line with that of national parliaments," it said.
